dedupe_keys.name: førde central hospital flood protection a 750 metre barrier and pumping station protecting old and new hospital buildings norway

description: This case describes how Førde Central Hospital in western Norway, built on a river delta and flooded in 2014, protected its whole site against a 1000-year flood. It is published by Climate-ADAPT, the European Environment Agency's adaptation platform, from information supplied by the hospital trust Helse Førde. The content covers the hazard (rain and snowmelt floods on a delta between two rivers), the 2014 flood that damaged the site, the rule that only new buildings needed protection, and how a site-wide development plan with a flood risk assessment for 200-year and 1000-year events made it possible to protect the 1979 buildings too. The solution, finished in December 2020, is a 750-metre barrier of sheet piling, concrete walls and embankments with a four-pump station of 2 cubic metres per second on emergency power; it cost about NOK 50 million, set against an estimated NOK 5 billion to relocate the hospital, and its pumps started automatically in two floods since. The case is free and available to read online, with no data files to download. Caveats: it is a narrative account with reported costs, not a quantitative risk study, and coverage is one hospital site. Simulation uses: an example of protecting a critical facility against river flooding, with costs and design standards to calibrate adaptation options for hospitals. Related records: the Binghamton hospital floodwall (case_study-lourdes-hospital-floodwall-binghamton) and the New Orleans veterans hospital rebuild (case_study-new-orleans-va-hospital-flood-resilient-rebuild).

name: Førde Central Hospital flood protection: a 750-metre barrier and pumping station protecting old and new hospital buildings, Norway
organisations: Norwegian Water Resources and Energy Directorate
outcomes: A 750 m barrier of sheet piling, concrete walls and embankments and a four-pump station (2 m3/s) with emergency power, completed December 2020 for NOK 50 million, protects about 70,000 m2 of old and new buildings against a 1000-year flood; pumps started automatically in two later floods, most recently March 2025.

resources_used: Flood risk assessment for 200-year and 1000-year floods
Guidance from the Norwegian Water Resources and Energy Directorate

sources.note: Full case text: hospital on a river delta, buildings from 1979; 200-year flood in 2014 damaged the site; flood risk assessment for 200 and 1000-year events; objective to protect about 50,000 m2 existing and 20,000 m2 new buildings; 750 m system of sheet piling, concrete walls and embankments; pumping station with four pumps, 2 m3/s, emergency power; completed December 2020; two floods since, most recently March 2025, pumps started automatically; investment about NOK 50 million against relocation estimated at NOK 5 billion; maintenance NOK 1 to 2 million a year; published in Climate-ADAPT 19 June 2025

study_period: 2014 flood and concept design; completed December 2020; published June 2025
